cards.text: Habakkuk the prophet has spent this whole book going back and forth with the LORD. Now he does something different. This is a prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.

cards.question: Habakkuk starts by telling the LORD he has heard the report of His deeds. How does that report leave him?
Habakkuk wants the LORD's great deeds to stay in the history books. True or false?
Habakkuk asks the LORD, even in His wrath, to remember ___.

cards.text: Then the prayer turns into a picture: God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah.

cards.question: As God comes from Teman, how far does His glory reach?

cards.text: His radiance was like the sunlight, with rays flashing from His hand. Friend, I can't look at my own oven light too long, and that thing is forty watts on a good day.

cards.question: Habakkuk says God's power is hidden in His hand. True or false?

cards.text: Habakkuk keeps watching God come. And He doesn't travel alone.

cards.question: In Habakkuk's picture, what goes before God and follows in His steps?

cards.text: He stood and measured the earth, He looked, and He startled the nations. Just a LOOK, friend, and I've been staring down my oven timer for years without it flinching once.

cards.question: In this picture, the ancient mountains and the perpetual hills stay standing. True or false?
Mountains that seemed to last forever fall, but Habakkuk says God's ways are ___.

cards.text: Then the prophet says he saw the tents of Cushan and the curtains of Midian.

cards.question: What's happening at the tents of Cushan and the curtains of Midian?

cards.text: Now the prophet talks to the LORD directly, and of COURSE Habakkuk has questions: "Were You angry at the rivers, O LORD? Was Your wrath against the streams?"

cards.question: The LORD rides on His horses, and Habakkuk names His chariots after what they bring: chariots of ___.

cards.text: The LORD brandishes His bow, calls for many arrows, and splits the earth with rivers. Me? I brandish a rolling pin and the dough just sits there looking at me.

cards.question: When the mountains see the LORD, they stay calm. True or false?
Torrents of water sweep by, and Habakkuk pictures the deep like a person. What does the deep do?

cards.text: Even the sun and moon react, at the flash of the LORD's flying arrows and the brightness of His shining spear.

cards.question: At the flash of the LORD's arrows, the sun and moon race across the sky. True or false?

cards.text: Then the prophet says, "You marched across the earth with fury; You threshed the nations in wrath."

cards.question: All that marching has a purpose. Why does the LORD go forth?

cards.text: The LORD crushes the head of the house of the wicked and strips him from head to toe. Selah.

cards.question: When the wicked one's warriors storm out to scatter Habakkuk's people, what does the LORD pierce his head with?
Habakkuk says those warriors came out gloating, as though ready to secretly devour the strong. True or false?
Habakkuk's battle picture circles back to where his questions began. With His horses, the LORD tramples the ___.

cards.text: Habakkuk has heard all of it. Now he tells what it does to him, from the inside out.

cards.question: What happens inside Habakkuk when he hears it all?

cards.text: His lips quiver at the sound, decay enters his bones, and he trembles where he stands. I know that one, friend: years in a junk drawer, holding my breath every time it rattled open, mustache shaking like a leaf.

cards.question: Shaking or not, Habakkuk says he must wait patiently for the day of distress to come upon the ___.

cards.text: Then comes the big though: though the fig tree doesn't bud, no fruit is on the vines, the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food. That's opening the cookie box and finding nothing but crumbs.

cards.question: In Habakkuk's list, the crops fail but the sheep and cattle are still safe. True or false?
Empty fields and empty stalls. What does Habakkuk say he will do anyway?
Habakkuk says he will rejoice in the God of his ___.

cards.text: Though there's no fruit, no crop and no cattle, this man says he will REJOICE. Friend, I once pulled ONE burnt batch out of the oven and sulked for a week.

cards.question: Habakkuk says his strength comes from his own hard work. True or false?
GOD the Lord makes Habakkuk able to walk upon the heights. What animal's feet does He make Habakkuk's feet like?

cards.text: The prayer ends with a note for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments. The man who spent this whole book asking questions just handed the choir a song.

findings.problem: The card says Habakkuk 'has spent this whole book going back and forth with the LORD.' That is a fact from Habakkuk 1–2, outside the passage, but the card gives no reference for it and cites only Habakkuk 3:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question says Habakkuk 'has heard the report of His deeds.' The BSB says 'I have heard the report of You; I stand in awe, O LORD, of Your deeds.' The report is of the LORD, and the awe is of His deeds. The card merges the two and changes what the text calls the report.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'the past' is close to the right answer. In the same verse Habakkuk asks the LORD to revive His past deeds, and card 3 has just tested that. A baker could argue that Habakkuk is asking God to remember the past.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Cushan and Midian appear here for the first time, and the card never says who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card says 'Now the prophet talks to the LORD directly,' which suggests this is the first time. Habakkuk already speaks directly to the LORD in 3:2 ('O LORD, I have heard...'), and stop 1, card 2 even says he 'starts by telling the LORD.'

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'Chariots of ___' asks the baker to fill in the wording of the line. No earlier card points to 'salvation,' and 'fire' is just as reasonable a guess, so the blank tests the poem's wording, not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The BSB says 'With his own spear You pierced his head,' meaning the wicked one's own spear. The answer 'His own spear,' with a capital H, reads as the LORD's own spear, which the text shows is not right.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question says the battle picture 'circles back to where his questions began,' but stop 2, card 1 told only the rivers and streams questions and left out the sea (3:8). The baker has no setup that points to 'sea,' and the hint really points to rivers, which is not an option.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Question the LORD again' is something Habakkuk does in this passage: he questions the LORD in 3:8, and stop 2, card 1 points that out ('of COURSE Habakkuk has questions').

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The card retells 3:17–18 (no fruit, no crop, no cattle, he will rejoice), which cards 5 through 8 already covered. Apart from the joke, it doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells new material.

'The man who spent this whole book asking questions' stretches Habakkuk 1–2. Much of chapter 2 is the LORD's answer, not Habakkuk's questions. It is also a fact from outside the passage with no reference.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Of the 8 true-or-false cards, 7 have False as the right answer (stop 1, cards 3 and 12; stop 2, cards 4, 7 and 12; stop 3, cards 6 and 10). Only stop 1, card 8 is True. Several use the same 'X stays calm/standing' setup, so a baker can learn to pick False without reasoning.
findings.question: Should there be a rule about how true-or-false answers are balanced across a walkthrough, or against repeating the same negated-statement setup, so the right answer can't be predicted from a pattern?
